newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India drifts, seen quiet pre-budget.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India drifts, seen quiet pre-budget.

text.p: Indian Global Depositary Receipts were hardly changed in slow Friday trade amid low Asian activity as a result of market holidays.
Dealers said trade mirrored a lethargic Indian market, and activity was likely to be limited ahead of the February 28 budget.
"We should see things quiet and steady before the budget," a trader said.
He said some activity had been seen after VSNL said it had finalised an international syndicate for its proposed GDR issue. A spokesman said it was likely to take place in the first quarter of 1997.
Dealers said some prices had been squeezed up on relatively thin volumes. Hindalco added 37 cents to $24.00/$25.00, while Reliance eased two cents to $14.37/$15.12.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended 4.62 points up at 3,407.22.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.14 points or 0.20 percent up at 67.78, with the premium over the local market at 15.68 percent from 15.64 percent on Thursday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.06 points at 66.12 with a premium of 43.68 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan GDR Index finished down 0.47 points at 100.25, with a premium of 3.73 percent to the local market.
